:::{#thm-odds-simplified}

#### Simplified expressions for odds function

::: notes
Two equivalent expressions for the odds function are:
:::

$$
\ba
\oddsf{\pi} &= \frac{1}{\pi^{-1}-1}
\\ &= \invf{\pi^{-1}-1}
\ea
$$ {#eq-odds-reduced}

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exr-odds2}
Prove @thm-odds-simplified.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-odds2}
Starting from @def-odds-fn:

$$
\ba
\oddsf{\pi} &\eqdef \frac{\pi}{1-\pi}
&& \text{(definition of the odds function)}
\\
&= \frac{\pi}{1-\pi}\cdot\frac{\pi^{-1}}{\pi^{-1}}
&& \text{(multiply numerator and denominator by } \pi^{-1} \text{)}
\\
&= \frac{\pi\pi^{-1}}{(1-\pi)\pi^{-1}}
&& \text{(distribute multiplication across fraction)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{(1-\pi)\pi^{-1}}
&& \text{(simplify numerator: } \pi\pi^{-1}=1 \text{)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\pi^{-1}-\pi\pi^{-1}}
&& \text{(distribute } \pi^{-1} \text{ in denominator)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\pi^{-1}-1}
&& \text{(simplify } \pi\pi^{-1}=1 \text{ in denominator)}
\\
&= \invf{\pi^{-1}-1}
&& \text{(notation for reciprocal function)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-odds2-1}

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-odds-simplified}

#### Computing odds using the simplified expression

Suppose an event has probability $\pi = 0.25$.

Using the simplified expression from @thm-odds-simplified:

$$
\ba
\oddsf{0.25} &= \invf{0.25^{-1} - 1}
&& \text{(simplified odds expression)}
\\
&= \invf{4 - 1}
&& \text{(reciprocal: } 0.25^{-1} = 4 \text{)}
\\
&= \invf{3}
&& \text{(subtraction)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{3}
&& \text{(reciprocal)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-computing-odds-using-the-simplified-1}

Checking against the standard odds definition:

$$\oddsf{0.25} = \frac{0.25}{1 - 0.25} = \frac{0.25}{0.75} = \frac{1}{3}$$ {#eq-computing-odds-using-the-simplified-2}

Both formulas yield identical odds of $1/3$.
:::
